learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how Multinational Corporations (MNCs), technology, and liberalisation policies integrate countries, creating a globalized economy.

key_vocabulary.definition: The process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries through trade, investment, and technology.
A company that owns or controls production in more than one nation.
Investment made by MNCs in another country to buy assets like land, buildings, and machines.
Restrictions set up by the government (like taxes on imports) to regulate foreign trade and protect domestic industries.
Removing trade barriers or restrictions set by the government on foreign trade and foreign investment.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: MNCs don't just sell globally; they *produce* globally. An MNC might design a product in the USA, manufacture components in China (cheap manufacturing), assemble them in Mexico, and handle customer service in India (skilled, English-speaking engineers). This drastically cuts costs and maximizes profits.

Two main drivers: 1. Rapid improvement in Technology (container ships for cheap transport, internet/telecom for instant communication). 2. Liberalisation of foreign trade policies. In 1991, India removed heavy trade barriers, allowing foreign goods and companies to enter the Indian market freely.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🌐 Role of the WTO (World Trade Organization)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The WTO is an international organization whose aim is to liberalize international trade. It establishes rules regarding international trade and sees that these rules are obeyed. However, developed countries often unfairly keep trade barriers while forcing developing nations to remove theirs.

main_concepts.concept_title: ⚖️ The Impact: Struggle for a Fair Globalisation
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Impact is mixed. Pros: Greater choice for consumers, lower prices, higher quality, and new jobs in IT/Services. Cons: Small local producers (like toy makers or battery manufacturers) are wiped out by cheap imports, and workers face job insecurity as companies look for cheap, flexible labor.

fun_activity.title: 📱 The Smartphone Autopsy
fun_activity.instructions: Pick up your smartphone. Where is it from? The brand might be American (Apple) or South Korean (Samsung). The battery is likely mined in Congo, the microchip designed in Taiwan, the camera lens made in Japan, assembled in a massive factory in China, and sold to you in India. Your phone is the ultimate symbol of Globalisation!

exam_tips: 📌 SEZs (Special Economic Zones) are heavily tested. They are industrial zones set up by the government with world-class facilities and tax exemptions for 5 years to attract foreign companies.
📌 Distinguish between Foreign Trade (import/export of goods) and Foreign Investment (MNCs setting up factories or buying local companies).
📌 Remember that the 1991 economic reforms in India marked the shift from a heavily protected economy to a liberalised, globalised economy.
quick_recap: ⭐ The most common route for MNC investments is to buy up existing local companies and then expand production.
⭐ Fair globalisation would create opportunities for all and ensure that the benefits of globalisation are shared better.
⭐ Flexibility in labor laws allows companies to hire workers on short-term contracts, cutting costs but destroying job security for workers.
